source.text: וַתְּדַבֵּ֨ר מִרְיָ֤ם וְאַהֲרֹן֙ בְּמֹשֶׁ֔ה עַל־אֹד֛וֹת הָאִשָּׁ֥ה הַכֻּשִׁ֖ית אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקָ֑ח כִּֽי־אִשָּׁ֥ה כֻשִׁ֖ית לָקָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Miriam and Aaron against Moses on account of the woman the Cushite whom he had taken; for a woman Cushite he had taken.

en.L: And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses on account of the Cushite woman whom he had taken, for he had taken a Cushite woman.
en.B: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses on account of the Cushite woman he had married, since he had married a Cushite woman.
en.R: Miriam and Aaron began to criticize Moses because he had married a woman from Cush.

es.L: Y hablaron Miriam y Aarón contra Moisés a causa de la mujer cusita que había tomado, porque había tomado una mujer cusita.
es.B: Miriam y Aarón hablaron contra Moisés por causa de la mujer cusita con la que se había casado, pues se había casado con una cusita.
es.R: Miriam y Aarón empezaron a criticar a Moisés porque se había casado con una mujer de Cus.

fr.L: Et Myriam et Aaron parlèrent contre Moïse au sujet de la femme koushite qu’il avait prise, car il avait pris une femme koushite.
fr.B: Myriam et Aaron parlèrent contre Moïse au sujet de la femme koushite qu’il avait épousée, car il avait épousé une Koushite.
fr.R: Myriam et Aaron se sont mis à critiquer Moïse parce qu’il avait épousé une femme originaire de Koush.

sw.L: Na Miriamu na Haruni wakamnena Musa kwa sababu ya yule mwanamke Mkushi aliyekuwa amemtwaa, kwa maana alikuwa amemtwaa mwanamke Mkushi.
sw.B: Miriamu na Haruni walimsema Musa vibaya kwa sababu ya mwanamke Mkushi aliyekuwa amemwoa, kwa kuwa alikuwa amemwoa mwanamke Mkushi.
sw.R: Miriamu na Haruni walianza kumlaumu Musa kwa sababu alikuwa amemwoa mwanamke kutoka Kushi.

decisions.choice: Miriam spoke: the verb is feminine singular, so Miriam leads
decisions.reason: The verb "spoke" is in the feminine singular form, though both Miriam and Aaron are named. A verb placed first often agrees with the first name only, but here it also fits the story: Miriam is named first and is the one who is punished (verse 10). Aaron joins her and later confesses for both (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Cushite: a woman from Cush, probably the land south of Egypt
alternatives: Zipporah, called a Cushite as a Midianite
a second wife from the land of Cush
decisions.reason: Cush is usually the land on the Nile south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan (Genesis 10:6; Isaiah 18:1-2). Habakkuk 3:7 sets Cushan beside Midian, and Moses' wife Zipporah was a Midianite (Exodus 2:21), so some read this as Zipporah. The text does not say whether she is Zipporah or a second wife, and it does not say why her being a Cushite was held against Moses.

decisions.choice: had taken: had married
decisions.reason: To "take" a woman is the ordinary Hebrew way to say a man married her (Genesis 4:19; 24:67). The clause is repeated at the end of the verse to make plain the fact behind the complaint.

decisions.choice: spoke against: spoke in criticism of
decisions.reason: "Speak against" (literally "speak in" someone) means to speak critically of a person, as the people spoke against God and Moses in 21:5-7. Verse 8 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: married / had married
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "married", the sense of "taken" here. Readable states the complaint once; Balanced keeps the repeated clause, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: "cusita", "Cus" for the Cushite woman and her land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Cush, the land on the Nile south of Egypt (meaning decision m2), spelled "Cus" as in Genesis 10. "Etíope" would point to the modern country, whose borders are not those of ancient Cush.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("parlèrent", "descendit"); passé composé at Readable ("se sont mis à critiquer"); the LORD's words keep the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level.

decisions.choice: "koushite", "Koush" for the Cushite woman and her land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Cush, the land on the Nile south of Egypt (meaning decision m2), and "Koush" is the spelling used for it in Genesis 10. "Éthiopienne", the older rendering from the Greek, now names a modern country with different borders.

decisions.choice: "Mkushi", "Kushi" for the Cushite woman and her land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Cush, the land on the Nile south of Egypt (meaning decision m2), spelled "Kushi" as in Genesis 10. "Mwethiopia" would point to the modern country of Ethiopia.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ הֲרַ֤ק אַךְ־בְּמֹשֶׁה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲלֹ֖א גַּם־בָּ֣נוּ דִבֵּ֑ר וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, only indeed by Moses has spoken Yahweh? not also by us has he spoken? And heard Yahweh.

en.L: And they said, "[Is it] only, indeed, by Moses [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken? [Is it] not by us also [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard [it].
en.B: "Is it only through Moses that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken?" they said. "Has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not spoken through us too?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard it.
en.R: They said, "Is Moses the only one {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken through? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken through us too!" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard what they said.

es.L: Y dijeron: «¿[Es que] solamente, de veras, por medio de Moisés ha hablado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}? ¿No ha hablado también por medio de nosotros?». Y [lo] oyó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: «¿Acaso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado solo por medio de Moisés? —decían—. ¿No ha hablado también por medio de nosotros?». Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo oyó.
es.R: Decían: «¿Es Moisés el único por medio del cual ha hablado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}? ¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} también ha hablado por medio de nosotros!». Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} oyó lo que decían.

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « [Est-ce] seulement, vraiment, par Moïse [que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé ? N’a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas aussi parlé par nous ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [l’]entendit.
fr.B: « Est-ce seulement par Moïse que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé ? disaient-ils. N’a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas parlé aussi par nous ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’entendit.
fr.R: Ils disaient : « Est-ce que Moïse est le seul par qui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé ? {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé par nous aussi ! » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a entendu ce qu’ils disaient.

sw.L: Wakasema, "Je, kweli {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema kupitia Musa tu? Je, hajasema kupitia sisi pia?" Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasikia.
sw.B: Walisema, "Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema kupitia Musa peke yake? Je, hajasema kupitia sisi pia?" Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasikia.
sw.R: Walisema, "Je, Musa ndiye peke yake ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema kupitia kwake? {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema kupitia sisi pia!" Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasikia waliyoyasema.

decisions.choice: two questions that expect the answers "no" and "yes"
decisions.reason: The first question, made stronger by two words for "only", expects the answer "no"; the second, "has he not?", expects "yes". Miriam and Aaron claim that the LORD speaks through them as well as through Moses. Miriam is called a prophet in Exodus 15:20, and Aaron spoke for Moses in Exodus 4:15-16.

decisions.choice: by: through, by means of
decisions.reason: The preposition here means the one through whom the LORD speaks his message, not the one he speaks to. The question is about who is the LORD's spokesperson. 2 Samuel 23:2 uses the same expression.

decisions.choice: the LORD heard: he took note of what was said against Moses
decisions.reason: The short statement prepares for what follows: the LORD hears what is said in the camp and acts on it, as in 11:1.

decisions.choice: The LORD has spoken through us too!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the second question, which expects "yes", into a plain statement, because a question with "not" can confuse young readers. It names the LORD instead of "he" for clarity.

source.text: וְהָאִ֥ישׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה עָנָ֣יו מְאֹ֑ד מִכֹּל֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the man Moses [was] humble very, more than all the human[s] who [were] on [the] face of the ground.

en.L: And the man Moses [was] very humble, more than any human being who [was] on the face of the ground.
en.B: Now Moses was exceedingly humble, more so than any other human being on earth.
en.R: Moses was a very humble man. No one else on earth was as humble as he was.

es.L: Y el hombre Moisés [era] muy humilde, más que todo ser humano que [había] sobre la faz de la tierra.
es.B: Ahora bien, Moisés era sumamente humilde, más que cualquier otro ser humano sobre la tierra.
es.R: Moisés era un hombre muy humilde. No había nadie en la tierra tan humilde como él.

fr.L: Or l’homme Moïse [était] très humble, plus que tout être humain qui [était] sur la face de la terre.
fr.B: Or Moïse était un homme extrêmement humble, plus que tout autre être humain sur la terre.
fr.R: Moïse était un homme très humble. Personne d’autre sur la terre n’était aussi humble que lui.

sw.L: Na yule mtu Musa [alikuwa] mnyenyekevu sana, kuliko mwanadamu yeyote aliyekuwa juu ya uso wa nchi.
sw.B: Basi Musa alikuwa mnyenyekevu mno, kuliko mwanadamu mwingine yeyote duniani.
sw.R: Musa alikuwa mtu mnyenyekevu sana. Hakuna mtu mwingine duniani aliyekuwa mnyenyekevu kama yeye.

decisions.choice: humble: the word as read, though the written form has an extra letter
decisions.reason: The traditional written text spells this word with an extra yod, a form that looks like a plural, while the scribes' note gives the reading for a singular adjective. Both point to the same word, "humble", and the meaning is not in doubt. Reviewers should check the note against the Westminster Leningrad Codex.

decisions.choice: humble: lowly, not claiming status for oneself
decisions.reason: The word describes someone who is lowly, often poor or afflicted, and who depends on God rather than on his own standing (Psalm 37:11; Zephaniah 2:3). Here it explains why Moses does not answer the charge: he does not defend himself, and the LORD speaks for him (verses 4-8). It is not a word for weakness.

decisions.choice: a comment by the narrator, set between the complaint and the LORD's answer
decisions.reason: The verse begins with "now" and the subject, not the usual word for "and then", so it steps out of the story to tell the reader about Moses. It explains why Moses says nothing in his own defense.

decisions.choice: more so than any other human being / no one else
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the comparison with all other people plain. The Hebrew word for a human being covers men and women alike, and the English wording does too.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה פִּתְאֹ֗ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶל־מִרְיָ֔ם צְא֥וּ שְׁלָשְׁתְּכֶ֖ם אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh suddenly to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam, come out, [the] three of you, to [the] tent of meeting; and came out [the] three of them.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said suddenly to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam, "Go out, the three of you, to the tent of meeting." And the three of them went out.
en.B: Without warning {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, Aaron and Miriam: "You three, come out to the tent of meeting." And the three went out.
en.R: Right away {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, "All three of you, come out to the meeting tent." So the three of them went.

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de repente a Moisés, y a Aarón, y a Miriam: «{{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tres a la Tienda del Encuentro». Y salieron ellos tres.
es.B: Sin previo aviso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés, a Aarón y a Miriam: «{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} tres, {{plural_you:salgan|salid}} a la Tienda del Encuentro». Y salieron los tres.
es.R: Enseguida {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dijo a Moisés, a Aarón y a Miriam: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} los tres a la Tienda del Encuentro». Y fueron los tres.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit soudain à Moïse, et à Aaron, et à Myriam : « Sortez, vous trois, vers la tente de la Rencontre. » Et ils sortirent, eux trois.
fr.B: Sans prévenir, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse, à Aaron et à Myriam : « Vous trois, sortez vers la tente de la Rencontre. » Et ils sortirent tous les trois.
fr.R: Aussitôt, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse, à Aaron et à Myriam : « Venez tous les trois à la tente de la Rencontre. » Alors ils y sont allés tous les trois.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia ghafula Musa, na Haruni, na Miriamu, "Tokeni, ninyi watatu, mwende kwenye Hema la Kukutania." Nao wakatoka wao watatu.
sw.B: Ghafula {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaambia Musa, Haruni na Miriamu, "Ninyi watatu, tokeni mje kwenye Hema la Kukutania." Nao watatu wakatoka.
sw.R: Mara moja {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaambia Musa, Haruni na Miriamu, "Njooni nyote watatu kwenye Hema la Kukutania." Basi wote watatu wakaenda.

decisions.choice: suddenly: at once, without warning
decisions.reason: The word means something that happens all at once, often as a surprise (Joshua 10:9; Isaiah 29:5). The LORD answers the complaint straight away.

decisions.choice: come out to the tent of meeting: out of the camp, where the tent stood
decisions.reason: In this part of Numbers the tent of meeting is where the LORD meets Moses, and people "go out" to it (11:24-26), as in Exodus 33:7. The three are summoned to the place where the LORD will speak and judge.

decisions.choice: Without warning / Right away
decisions.reason: "Suddenly" before "said" can sound odd in English; Balanced says "without warning" and Readable "right away", which keep the sense that the LORD answered at once.

source.text: וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהוָה֙ בְּעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֔ן וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וַיִּקְרָא֙ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וּמִרְיָ֔ם וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came down Yahweh in [a] pillar of cloud and stood [at the] entrance of the tent and called Aaron and Miriam, and came out [the] two of them.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Aaron and Miriam; and they went out, the two of them.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came down in a pillar of cloud and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} stand at the entrance of the tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came down in a tall cloud and stood at the door of the tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and they both came forward.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} descendió en una columna de nube y se puso a la entrada de la tienda, y llamó a Aarón y a Miriam; y salieron ellos dos.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} descendió en una columna de nube y se detuvo a la entrada de la tienda. Llamó a Aarón y a Miriam, y los dos se adelantaron.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bajó en una nube alta y se paró a la puerta de la tienda. Llamó a Aarón y a Miriam, y los dos se acercaron.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} descendit dans une colonne de nuée et se tint à l’entrée de la tente, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela Aaron et Myriam ; et ils sortirent, eux deux.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} descendit dans une colonne de nuée et se tint à l’entrée de la tente. Il appela Aaron et Myriam, et tous deux s’avancèrent.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est descendu dans un grand nuage et s’est arrêté à l’entrée de la tente. Il a appelé Aaron et Myriam, et ils se sont avancés tous les deux.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akashuka katika nguzo ya wingu, akasimama mlangoni pa hema, akawaita Haruni na Miriamu; nao wakatoka wote wawili.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alishuka katika nguzo ya wingu, akasimama mlangoni pa hema. Akawaita Haruni na Miriamu, nao wawili wakajitokeza mbele.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alishuka katika wingu refu, akasimama mlangoni pa hema. Akawaita Haruni na Miriamu, nao wote wawili wakasogea mbele.

decisions.choice: came down in a pillar of cloud: the LORD made his presence seen
decisions.reason: The pillar of cloud is the sign of the LORD's presence that led Israel and stood at the tent (Exodus 13:21; 33:9-10). "Came down" describes the LORD coming near to act, as in 11:25.

decisions.choice: came out: stepped forward from beside Moses
decisions.reason: All three had already come out to the tent (verse 4). Now only Aaron and Miriam are called, so here "came out" means they stepped forward to face the LORD, apart from Moses.

decisions.choice: a tall cloud
decisions.reason: Readable describes the pillar as a tall cloud, since "pillar" is a less common word for young readers. It is the same cloud as elsewhere in the story.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֣א דְבָרָ֑י אִם־יִֽהְיֶה֙ נְבִ֣יאֲכֶ֔ם יְהוָ֗ה בַּמַּרְאָה֙ אֵלָ֣יו אֶתְוַדָּ֔ע בַּחֲל֖וֹם אֲדַבֶּר־בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, hear please my words: if there is your prophet, Yahweh, in the vision to him I make myself known, in a dream I speak with him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Hear now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words: \q if there is a prophet of yours, \q [I,] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in a vision make {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known to him; \q in a dream I speak with him.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Hear what I say: \q whenever you have a prophet, \q I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, make {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known to him in a vision; \q in a dream I speak with him.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Listen to what I say: \q if you have a prophet, I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to him in a vision, or I speak to him in a dream.

es.L: Y dijo: «{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} ahora {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras: \q si hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un profeta, \q [yo,] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, en visión {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} doy a conocer a él; \q en sueños hablo con él.
es.B: Luego dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} lo que digo: \q siempre que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} un profeta, \q yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} doy a conocer a él en una visión; \q en un sueño hablo con él.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: \q si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} un profeta, yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} muestro a él en una visión, o le hablo en un sueño.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Écoutez donc {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles : \q s’il y a parmi vous un prophète, \q [moi,] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en vision je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fais connaître de lui ; \q en songe je parle avec lui.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Écoutez ce que je dis : \q quand vous avez un prophète, \q moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fais connaître à lui dans une vision ; \q dans un songe je lui parle.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : « Écoutez ce que je vais vous dire : \q si vous avez un prophète, moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} montre à lui dans une vision, ou je lui parle dans un rêve.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Sikieni sasa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}: \q ikiwa yupo nabii wenu, \q [{{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}},] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, katika maono hujijulisha kwake; \q katika ndoto husema naye.
sw.B: Kisha akasema, "Sikilizeni ninayosema: \q kila mnapokuwa na nabii, \q {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, hujijulisha kwake katika maono; \q katika ndoto husema naye.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema, "Sikilizeni ninachowaambia: \q ikiwa mna nabii, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, hujionyesha kwake katika maono, au husema naye katika ndoto.

decisions.choice: your prophet, the LORD: "I, the LORD", the speaker naming himself
alternatives: if there is a prophet of the LORD among you
decisions.reason: The words run "your prophet, the LORD, in a vision ...". The marks in the traditional text join "the LORD" to what follows, so the LORD names himself as the one who makes himself known: "I, the LORD". Another way to read it is "a prophet of the LORD among you". The sense of the verse is the same either way.

decisions.choice: vision, dream: the usual ways God speaks to prophets
decisions.reason: Visions and dreams are the ordinary means by which God gives his word to prophets (Genesis 46:2; Joel 3:1; Daniel 7:1). They need explaining, which is the contrast with Moses in verse 8.

decisions.choice: if there is: whenever there is, a general rule
decisions.reason: The verse states a general rule about prophets, not a doubt about whether any exist.

decisions.choice: whenever you have a prophet
decisions.reason: Balanced says "whenever" because the verse states a general rule; Literal and Readable keep "if". "You have a prophet" follows the Hebrew "your prophet".

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, because "he" at the start of the speech could be taken for Moses or Aaron.

source.text: לֹא־כֵ֖ן עַבְדִּ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה בְּכָל־בֵּיתִ֖י נֶאֱמָ֥ן הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Not so my servant Moses; in all my house faithful [is] he.

en.L: Not so {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Moses; \q in all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house he [is] faithful.
en.B: It is not so with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses; \q he is trusted in all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} household.
en.R: But it is different with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses. \q He is the one I trust with everything in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} household.

es.L: No así {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo Moisés; \q en toda {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa él [es] fiel.
es.B: No sucede así con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Moisés; \q a él le he confiado toda {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa.
es.R: Pero con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Moisés es diferente. \q Él es aquel a quien le confío todo en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa.

fr.L: Il n’en est pas ainsi de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave Moïse ; \q dans toute {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison, il [est] fidèle.
fr.B: Il n’en va pas ainsi de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Moïse : \q c’est à lui que je confie toute {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison.
fr.R: Mais avec {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Moïse, c’est différent. \q C’est à lui que je confie tout ce qui concerne {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison.

sw.L: Sivyo [ilivyo kwa] mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Musa; \q katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yote yeye [ni] mwaminifu.
sw.B: Sivyo ilivyo kwa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Musa; \q yeye ameaminiwa katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yote.
sw.R: Lakini kwa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Musa ni tofauti. \q Yeye ndiye ninayemwamini kwa kila kitu katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: my servant: one who belongs to the LORD and acts for him
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a slave, a person owned by a master and under his authority, not hired help. Applied to Moses (Exodus 14:31; Deuteronomy 34:5), it is a title of honor: he belongs wholly to the LORD and carries out his business.

decisions.choice: faithful in all my house: trusted with the whole household
decisions.reason: The verb form means proved reliable and so trusted. A trusted servant was put in charge of his master's whole household (Genesis 24:2; 39:4-6). The LORD's house here is his people and all his affairs with them. Hebrews 3:2-5 takes up this verse.

decisions.choice: not so: Moses is the exception to the rule just stated
decisions.reason: The short opening sets Moses apart from the prophets of verse 6: the LORD does not deal with him by visions and dreams.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal) / servant; faithful (Literal) / trusted
decisions.reason: Literal says "slave" and Balanced and Readable "servant", as in Exodus. Balanced says "trusted" because in English "faithful" can suggest only that Moses is loyal, while the point is that the LORD has put him in charge.

source.text: פֶּ֣ה אֶל־פֶּ֞ה אֲדַבֶּר־בּ֗וֹ וּמַרְאֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א בְחִידֹ֔ת וּתְמֻנַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה יַבִּ֑יט וּמַדּ֨וּעַ֙ לֹ֣א יְרֵאתֶ֔ם לְדַבֵּ֖ר בְּעַבְדִּ֥י בְמֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Mouth to mouth I speak with him, and [in] sight and not in riddles, and [the] form of Yahweh he beholds; and why not were you afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?

en.L: Mouth to mouth I speak with him, and plainly and not in riddles, \q and the form of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} he looks on. \q And why were you not afraid \q to speak against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave, against Moses?"
en.B: I speak with him mouth to mouth, openly and not in riddles, \q and he looks on the form of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q How is it, then, that you were not afraid \q to speak against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses?"
en.R: I speak with him directly, clearly and not in puzzles, and he sees the form of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q So why were you not afraid to speak against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses?"

es.L: Boca a boca hablo con él, y claramente y no en enigmas, \q y la forma {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contempla él. \q ¿Y por qué no {{plural_you:tuvieron|tuvisteis}} temor \q de hablar contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo, contra Moisés?».
es.B: Con él hablo boca a boca, abiertamente y no en enigmas, \q y él contempla la forma {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q ¿Cómo es, entonces, que no {{plural_you:tuvieron|tuvisteis}} miedo \q de hablar contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Moisés?».
es.R: Hablo con él directamente, con claridad y no con adivinanzas, y él ve la forma {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q Entonces, ¿por qué no {{plural_you:tuvieron|tuvisteis}} miedo de hablar contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Moisés?».

fr.L: Bouche à bouche je parle avec lui, et clairement et non par énigmes, \q et il contemple la forme {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Et pourquoi n’avez-vous pas craint \q de parler contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave, contre Moïse ? »
fr.B: Je lui parle bouche à bouche, ouvertement et non par énigmes, \q et il contemple la forme {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Comment donc n’avez-vous pas craint \q de parler contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Moïse ? »
fr.R: Je lui parle directement, clairement et sans devinettes, et il voit la forme {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Alors pourquoi n’avez-vous pas eu peur de parler contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Moïse ? »

sw.L: Kinywa kwa kinywa nasema naye, waziwazi wala si kwa mafumbo, \q na umbo la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yeye hulitazama. \q Basi kwa nini hamkuogopa \q kumnena mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kumnena Musa?"
sw.B: Ninasema naye kinywa kwa kinywa, waziwazi wala si kwa mafumbo, \q naye hutazama umbo la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Imekuwaje basi hamkuogopa \q kumsema vibaya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Musa?"
sw.R: Ninasema naye moja kwa moja, kwa wazi wala si kwa vitendawili, naye huona umbo la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Basi kwa nini hamkuogopa kumsema vibaya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Musa?"

decisions.choice: mouth to mouth: directly, in person
decisions.reason: The phrase means speaking directly, without anyone or anything between, like "face to face" in Exodus 33:11 and Deuteronomy 34:10. Jeremiah 32:4 uses it of a king speaking in person.

decisions.choice: in sight, not in riddles: plainly, not in sayings that need decoding
decisions.reason: "Sight" here means seeing plainly, the opposite of riddles, which are dark sayings whose meaning must be worked out (Judges 14:12; Ezekiel 17:2). The same letters could be read as "in a vision", but the contrast with riddles favors "plainly". Either way the point is that the LORD's words to Moses are clear.

decisions.choice: the form of the LORD: a likeness of the LORD, not his full glory
decisions.reason: The word means a likeness or shape. Israel saw no form at Sinai (Deuteronomy 4:12, 15), but Moses is allowed to see more than others, as in Exodus 33:18-23, where he sees the LORD's back and not his face. The verse marks Moses' unique closeness to the LORD without saying he saw God fully.

decisions.choice: why were you not afraid: a rebuke, not a question looking for an answer
decisions.reason: The question accuses Miriam and Aaron: knowing all this, they should have feared to speak against Moses. The repeated "against" before "my servant" and "Moses" stresses who it was they spoke against.

decisions.choice: directly / puzzles
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture "mouth to mouth" as "directly" and says "puzzles" for riddles, sayings whose meaning has to be worked out.

decisions.choice: against my servant Moses
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated "against"; Balanced and Readable say it once, as English normally does, and the stress falls on "my servant".

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against them, and he went.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away.
en.B: The anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blazed against them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} departed.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away.

decisions.choice: the anger burned: he became fiercely angry
decisions.reason: The word for anger is also the word for "nose", and the picture is of hot, flaring anger (Exodus 4:14; Numbers 11:1, 10, 33). It is the LORD's response to what Miriam and Aaron said against his servant.

decisions.choice: he went away: the LORD withdrew his presence
decisions.reason: The LORD had come down in the cloud to judge (verse 5). His leaving is seen in the next verse, when the cloud lifts from the tent, and only then is the judgment seen.

decisions.choice: was very angry with them
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of burning anger means.

source.text: וְהֶעָנָ֗ן סָ֚ר מֵעַ֣ל הָאֹ֔הֶל וְהִנֵּ֥ה מִרְיָ֖ם מְצֹרַ֣עַת כַּשָּׁ֑לֶג וַיִּ֧פֶן אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶל־מִרְיָ֖ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה מְצֹרָֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the cloud turned from over the tent, and behold, Miriam [was] struck with scale disease like snow; and turned Aaron to Miriam, and behold, [she was] struck with scale disease.

en.L: And the cloud turned away from over the tent, and look, Miriam [was] struck with scale disease, like snow; and Aaron turned toward Miriam, and look, [she was] struck with scale disease.
en.B: As the cloud withdrew from above the tent, there was Miriam, stricken with a serious skin disease, like snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam, and there she was with the disease.
en.R: When the cloud left the tent, Miriam suddenly had a serious skin disease. Her skin looked like snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw what had happened to her.

decisions.choice: struck with scale disease: a skin disease that made a person unclean, not modern leprosy
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in Leviticus 13-14 for skin conditions with visible signs that made a person unclean and kept them outside the camp (Leviticus 13:45-46; Numbers 5:2). It is not the same as leprosy as known today (Hansen's disease).

decisions.choice: like snow: white, or flaking like snow
decisions.reason: The comparison may describe the white color of the diseased skin (Leviticus 13:3-4) or its flaking. The same words are used of Moses' hand in Exodus 4:6 and of Gehazi in 2 Kings 5:27. Either way it is a sudden and visible sign of judgment.

decisions.choice: and look: what is suddenly seen
decisions.reason: The word marks something seen all at once, here first by the narrator and then through Aaron's eyes. The disease appears the moment the cloud lifts.

decisions.choice: only Miriam is struck
decisions.reason: Aaron is not struck, though he spoke too. The text gives no reason. Miriam took the lead (verse 1), and Aaron as priest could not have served while unclean (Leviticus 21:16-23; 22:4); Aaron instead confesses for both (verse 11).

decisions.choice: a serious skin disease / had the disease
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "serious skin disease", as in Leviticus 13, rather than "leprosy". Literal keeps "scale disease". Balanced says "there was" and "there she was" for the word "look"; Readable uses "suddenly" and "saw".

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אַהֲרֹ֖ן אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י אַל־נָ֨א תָשֵׁ֤ת עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ חַטָּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר נוֹאַ֖לְנוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָֽאנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Aaron to Moses, please my lord, do not please put on us [the] sin which we have acted foolishly and which we have sinned.

en.L: And Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not, please, lay on us the sin [in] which we have acted foolishly and [in] which we have sinned.
en.B: Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not make us bear the penalty for the sin we committed in our foolishness.
en.R: Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not make us suffer for our sin. We have acted foolishly, and we have done wrong.

decisions.choice: please, my lord: a humble plea to a superior
decisions.reason: "Please" here is a word used to begin an urgent request (Genesis 43:20; 44:18). "My lord" is a polite address to someone of higher rank. Aaron is Moses' older brother (Exodus 7:7), yet he now speaks to him as one who has power to help.

decisions.choice: lay sin on us: make us bear the punishment for the sin
decisions.reason: The word for sin can include its penalty. To "put" or "lay" a sin on someone is to hold them guilty and let the punishment fall on them. Aaron asks Moses to pray that it not be counted against them.

decisions.choice: acted foolishly and sinned: two words that admit the wrong
decisions.reason: The first verb means to act like a fool, without sense (1 Samuel 13:13; Jeremiah 5:4). Aaron uses both verbs to admit fully that what they said against Moses was wrong.

decisions.choice: the sin we committed in our foolishness
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two clauses "which we have acted foolishly and which we have sinned" into one, because the two say the same thing about the one sin.

source.text: אַל־נָ֥א תְהִ֖י כַּמֵּ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּצֵאתוֹ֙ מֵרֶ֣חֶם אִמּ֔וֹ וַיֵּאָכֵ֖ל חֲצִ֥י בְשָׂרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not please let her be like the dead [one], who when coming out from [the] womb of his mother, and is eaten half of his flesh.

en.L: Please do not let her be like the dead [one] who, at his coming out from his mother's womb, has half his flesh eaten away."
en.B: Do not let her be like a child born dead, half its flesh already wasted when it leaves its mother's womb."
en.R: Please do not let her be like a baby that is dead when it is born, with half of its body already decayed."

decisions.choice: the dead one: a stillborn child
decisions.reason: The picture is of a child born dead, its skin and flesh already decaying. Aaron compares Miriam's diseased skin to this: she is like someone dead while still alive, cut off from the camp and the people.

decisions.choice: his mother, his flesh: the received text
decisions.reason: Jewish tradition lists this verse among a few places where scribes are said to have changed the wording out of respect, and says the earlier wording was "our mother" and "our flesh", making Miriam's suffering that of her own brothers. The traditional text read here has "his mother" and "his flesh". Reviewers should check this note.

decisions.choice: a child born dead / a baby that is dead when it is born
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the dead one who comes out of his mother's womb" refers to. They say "its" for the child, which is not a particular boy.

source.text: וַיִּצְעַ֣ק מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֵ֕ל נָ֛א רְפָ֥א נָ֖א לָֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And cried out Moses to Yahweh, saying, God, please, heal please her.

en.L: And Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "God, please, heal her, please!"
en.B: So Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "O God, please heal her!"
en.R: So Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Please heal her, God! Please!"

decisions.choice: God: the general word for God, in a short cry
decisions.reason: Moses calls on God with the short word for God, not the divine name. The prayer is only a few words, with "please" twice, the cry of someone pleading urgently.

decisions.choice: Moses prays for the one who spoke against him
decisions.reason: Moses does not defend himself (verse 3); now he pleads for Miriam. The LORD is the one who heals (Exodus 15:26).

decisions.choice: please (once)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps both words for "please" in the Hebrew order, and Readable keeps both as two short cries. Balanced says it once, with "O" for the urgent cry, because repeating it in one short sentence sounds unnatural.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה וְאָבִ֨יהָ֙ יָרֹ֤ק יָרַק֙ בְּפָנֶ֔יהָ הֲלֹ֥א תִכָּלֵ֖ם שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים תִּסָּגֵ֞ר שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְאַחַ֖ר תֵּאָסֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, and her father spitting had spit in her face, not would she be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut up seven days outside of the camp, and afterward she will be gathered.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "And her father, [if he] had spit, spit in her face, would she not be put to shame seven days? Let her be shut up seven days outside the camp, and afterward she may be gathered [back]."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "If her father had merely spit in her face, would she not carry her shame for seven days? She must be shut outside the camp seven days; then she may be taken back in."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, she would be ashamed for seven days. So she must stay outside the camp for seven days. Then she may be taken back in."

decisions.choice: spit in her face: a public insult that brought shame
decisions.reason: Spitting in someone's face was a sign of contempt and disgrace (Deuteronomy 25:9; Isaiah 50:6; Job 30:10). The Hebrew doubles the verb ("spitting had spit") for emphasis: if even that had happened, she would bear the shame.

decisions.choice: if ... would she not: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If a father's rebuke would leave her in disgrace for seven days, how much more a rebuke from the LORD. The question expects "yes".

decisions.choice: shut up outside the camp seven days: the period of confinement for skin disease
decisions.reason: The law of skin disease sets periods of seven days' confinement (Leviticus 13:4-5) and keeps the person outside the camp while unclean (Leviticus 13:46; Numbers 5:2-3). Seven days was also the time of uncleanness in other cases (Numbers 19:11).

decisions.choice: be gathered: be brought back into the camp
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather in or take back. Here it means Miriam will be received back into the community. The same verb is used of restoring someone from skin disease in 2 Kings 5:3, 6. The verse implies she will be healed.

decisions.choice: she would be ashamed
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question, which expects "yes", into a statement. Balanced and Literal keep the question.

source.text: וַתִּסָּגֵ֥ר מִרְיָ֛ם מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וְהָעָם֙ לֹ֣א נָסַ֔ע עַד־הֵאָסֵ֖ף מִרְיָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was shut up Miriam outside of the camp seven days, and the people not set out until was gathered Miriam.

en.L: And Miriam was shut up outside the camp seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was gathered [back].
en.B: So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not break camp until she had been taken back in.
en.R: So Miriam had to stay outside the camp for seven days. The people did not move on until she was taken back in.

decisions.choice: the people did not set out: the whole camp waited for Miriam
decisions.reason: The camp moved only when the cloud led it (9:17-23). Here it does not move on until Miriam is restored, so she is not left behind in the wilderness. Her punishment held up the whole people, but it also showed she remained one of them.

decisions.choice: was gathered: was brought back in
decisions.reason: As in verse 14: received back into the camp, clean.

decisions.choice: she had been taken back in
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "she" for the second "Miriam", since English rarely repeats a name in one sentence.

source.text: וְאַחַ֛ר נָסְע֥וּ הָעָ֖ם מֵחֲצֵר֑וֹת וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָֽן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And afterward set out the people from Hazeroth and camped in [the] wilderness of Paran.

en.L: And afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
en.B: After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
en.R: Then the people left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.

decisions.choice: Hazeroth, the wilderness of Paran: stages of the journey from Sinai
decisions.reason: Israel came to Hazeroth after Kibroth-hattaavah (11:35; 33:17). The wilderness of Paran, south of Canaan, is where the cloud first settled after Sinai (10:12), and it is from there that the spies are sent out in the next chapter (13:3, 26). Neither place can be located exactly today.

decisions.choice: Desert
decisions.reason: Readable says "desert" for the wilderness, a dry land with little rain and few people, as it does elsewhere.
